summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of the Offices CMS module. Backend: 18/18 pytest cases pass covering CRUD, uniqueness (409), validation (422 on missing/invalid lat/lon/radius), partial updates + updated_at, and bulk-delete. Frontend: full E2E via Playwright — page load, breadcrumb, table, empty-form validation, create + toast + row insert, duplicate 409 surfaced, search filter, empty-filtered state + clear search, row-actions edit (persists), row-actions delete + confirm dialog, select-all bulk delete + confirm, pagination footer visible, page-size dropdown works.
critical_code_review_comments: Route ordering in server.py is correct: /offices/bulk-delete is declared BEFORE /offices/{office_id} so it won't be swallowed by the path param — good.
_assert_unique detects field ('code' vs 'name') by comparing to the incoming value; correct and message includes the field name for the frontend to surface.
Consider adding a MongoDB unique index on offices.code and offices.name to enforce integrity at DB level (currently only application-level check — race conditions possible under concurrent inserts).

Office.update_one uses $set but does not return the updated doc from Mongo; the code merges `updates` into the local `doc` which works, but ReturnDocument.AFTER via find_one_and_update would be more robust.
OfficesPage.jsx is ~750 lines — consider splitting the OfficeFormDialog and column defs into their own files for maintainability.
seed_data_creation: During bulk-delete UI test the pre-existing HQ-01/Head Office seed row was deleted along with test rows. Recreated via curl at end: code=HQ-01, name=Head Office, telephone=021-555, address='Jl. Merdeka 1', radius=150.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Offices CMS module is fully working end-to-end. Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_offices.py (pytest, 18 tests). All frontend data-testids match implementation. Note: bulk-delete select-all deletes every row (including seeded HQ-01); a checkbox on the seeded row was included in 'select-all'. This is expected behavior; if desired, main agent could seed offices via startup event to guarantee HQ-01 persists across test cleanups.
